name: Rutin
short: Phlebotonics, class-wide (incl. rutosides; no rutin figure): slightly more adverse events than placebo, mostly gut upsets. Pregnancy safety unclear. Rat study: apigenin plus rutin raised paclitaxel.
text: Evidence on rutin itself is sparse. A 2020 Cochrane review of placebo-controlled trials of oral phlebotonics for chronic venous insufficiency (rutosides, hidrosmine and diosmine, calcium dobesilate, Centella asiatica, aminaftone, French maritime pine bark extract and grape seed extract) found that phlebotonics as a group probably increase adverse events slightly compared with placebo (risk ratio 1.14, 95% CI 1.02 to 1.27; 37 studies; 5789 participants), most often gastrointestinal disorders; the abstract says "rutosides" without saying which were tested (hydroxyethylrutosides, for example, are semisynthetic derivatives of rutin rather than rutin itself) and gives no separate figures. In a 6-week placebo-controlled trial in 18 healthy women, rutin by mouth caused no adverse changes in blood chemistry or liver function tests. In a Cochrane review of varicose veins in pregnancy, one trial of a rutoside in 69 women found no significant difference in side effects versus placebo, but the reviewers judged the data insufficient to assess safety in pregnancy. A safety review of Japanese sophora flower, a source of rutin, noted that some studies indicate rutin or quercetin may have potential for drug interactions, and in a rat study giving apigenin and rutin with oral paclitaxel raised paclitaxel blood levels, which the authors linked to P-glycoprotein (animal data; the abstract does not clearly separate the effect of rutin from that of apigenin).
